title: Maximum Segment Sum
statement: A delivery route reports the profit (possibly negative) of each stop. The company may run any nonempty contiguous part of the route. Find the largest total profit that a contiguous segment can earn.
The segment must contain at least one stop, so when every profit is negative the answer is the largest single profit.
inputFormat: The first line contains an integer `n`.
outputFormat: Print the maximum sum of a nonempty contiguous segment.
constraints: The answer can be as large as 2·10^14. Use a 64-bit integer type (long in Java/C#, long long in C++).

starter.output: the largest sum of a nonempty contiguous segment (may need 64-bit)

private.complexity: O(n) with Kadane's recurrence best_ending_here = max(a[i], best_ending_here + a[i]). O(n^2) prefix-sum pairs time out on the 200000-element hidden cases.
private.notes: Initialise with a[0], not 0, so an all-negative array returns its maximum element.
